# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 82

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** SHE 082 — Similitude 8, Chapter 5
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Disagreements

**1. Verse 4 — "and none of them wither" placement**
- EMET: "if any of them take root, and none of them wither, they shall live"
- LOGOS: "if any of them take root and none of them wither, they shall live"
- PNEUMA: "If any of them take root and don't wither, they will live"
- Minor punctuation and phrasing difference; all three capture the conditional logic.

**2. Verse 5 — "Repentance that does not bear fruit" — all agree**
- Consensus on this key phrase. PNEUMA adds "that proves their repentance is real" as explanatory gloss.

**3. Verse 7 — "proclaimed" vs. "preached"**
- EMET: "the seal was also preached to these"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "the seal was also proclaimed to these"
- Minor. "Proclaimed" is more formal; "preached" is more traditional.

**4. Verse 9 — "foremost among the righteous" vs. "most eminent among the righteous"**
- EMET: "foremost among the righteous"
- LOGOS: "most eminent among the righteous"
- PNEUMA: "the foremost among the righteous"
- Minor stylistic variation on the same Greek.

**5. Verse 9 — "fell asleep" vs. "died"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "fell asleep in the power and faith of the Son of God"
- PNEUMA: "died in the power and faith of the Son of God"
- PNEUMA abandons the euphemistic Greek koimēthentes (fell asleep). "Fell asleep" is the standard Christian term.

**6. Verse 11 — "benefit nothing" vs. "does them no good"**
- EMET: "he shall not benefit at all"
- LOGOS: "he shall benefit nothing at all"
- PNEUMA: "it does them no good at all"
- Minor stylistic variation; all convey the same meaning.

**Total disagreements: 6**
